verdicts.note: No abstract; standardisation and individualisation of the youth-to-adulthood transition across cohorts born 1903-1965 places it in the exposure-trend stream but nothing further is visible.
Pre-modern Chinese lineage demography; universal marriage regime described, arrangement not an exposure.
French-language version of the preceding record.
Canadian home-leaving by family structure of origin; two-thirds of 20-24 year olds live with a parent and parental divorce lowers it. Link 1, and a useful exposure-prevalence figure.
Migration and union dissolution among Puerto Rican women.
Gender preference and resource flows in Taiwan; C.3.f's wealth-flows question.
Co-residence choices of ELDERLY parents and adult children in Taiwan. The homonym, with the arrangement as outcome.
No abstract; 'Aging trends -- the Philippines' is decisive on the homonym.

State policy, mortality and fertility in northern Vietnam 1945-95, with the demography of succession and CO-RESIDENCE as a stated object. Both links appear in one study; full-text read to see whether either is estimated.

Comparative household formation rules in Europe and Asia, disputing the joint-East versus single-couple-West dichotomy. Theory for the configuration split, and a Wall 3 caution about cross-national family-system comparisons.
Parental cohabitation and children's economic wellbeing; co-residence here is of a parent with a partner.

No abstract. Urbanisation, HOUSEHOLD COMPOSITION and reproductive health in a South African city names both axes in the title but settles neither the configuration nor whether fertility is the outcome.
Book review of Thornton and Lin on social change and the family in Taiwan.
Employed parents' ratings of workplace family programmes.

UNECE Fertility and Family Survey country report for Norway, carrying household composition, the PARENTAL HOME, partnership formation and fertility in one instrument. A data source for the chapter rather than an estimate.
No abstract; reasons pregnant adolescents gave for not contracepting is decisive on subject.
Parenting stress and marital quality.
Family characteristics and the labour force status of older married Finnish women.

Marital fertility and stem-family household size and composition in rural Navarre 1860-1930, with a dependency ratio computed over co-resident members. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2 but the closest historical analogue of the extended-couple cell.
Parental divorce against earlier home-leaving and a preference for cohabitation, Dutch FFS. Driver to arrangement, then arrangement to union, in one dataset.
Third National Survey on Household Changes in Japan, reporting a RISE in the age of leaving the parental home alongside nuclearisation. Exposure trend in the extended arm's key setting.
Age at leaving home in the United States 1850-60; historical link 1.
Life cycle of the Chinese elderly in Shanghai and Zhejiang.
Services for children with chronic neurological disease living at home.

Chinese family size and structure since the 1950s, attributed to population policy and to the Cultural Revolution housing shortage. The arrow runs to the arrangement, and housing appears as its driver -- a C.2.c seam worth noting.
Men's resources and union formation in Sweden and the US.
Child labour in Pakistan. C.3.b's.
Intergenerational childrearing among adolescent mothers and grandmothers; the outcome is parental adaptation, not fertility.
UNECE FFS country report for Poland; household composition, parental home, partnerships and fertility in one survey. Data source.
UNECE FFS country report for the Netherlands, 1993. Data source; the Dutch FFS is behind several of this frame's link-1 analyses.
Caregiving stress of employed adult children with an impaired parent.
No abstract. 'Home or Alone: The Costs of Independent Living for Youth' is squarely the pre-launch construct and the cost framing is C.2.c's seam; full-text read to place it.

Living-apart-together couples in France, using the Family Situations and FFS surveys. A fourth arrangement the scope has not enumerated: partnered but not co-resident, which breaks the assumed union-to-coresidence equivalence.

Argues the residential household is an inadequate and misleading unit in Botswana because domestic groups are not necessarily co-resident. A measurement critique that bears directly on §9's ARRANGEMENT_MEASURE field.
Burdens of parenting and psychological distress.
Love attitudes across family life stages.
Book review of Chinese Families in the Post-Mao Era.
Old-age support and care in China, focused on living arrangements. The homonym.
Depressive symptoms and alcohol problems.

Gender differences in household formation and housing demand in Canadian cities, projecting that women's rising income prospects will REDUCE family formation and fertility and change housing demand. Runs from fertility to housing; C.2.c cross-reference.
Sources and methods for rural Liaoning population history.
Economic analysis of Japanese population ageing.
Beijing household size decline, 80% attributed to fewer children. Fertility to household size.
Proto-industrialisation, population growth and family formation. Pre-modern theory; A.7's under Ruling 2.
Female role change among the Negev Bedouin after resettlement.
Living arrangements and social support of older persons in Egypt. The homonym.
Untitled symposium proceedings on universities in developing areas.
Marriage and migration in Malaysia; moves before and during marriage, no arrangement-with-parents exposure.
Early life courses of Canadian men, sequencing school exit, work entry, leaving the parental home and family formation. Sequence description.
No abstract; early life transitions of Canadian women, timing and sequences, is the companion to the preceding record.
Adult children's closeness with parents; coresidency is one reviewed correlate of contact.
Predictors of marital interaction in 20 couples.
UNECE FFS country report for Latvia; same instrument family as the Norway, Poland and Netherlands reports. Data source.
Twentieth-century decline in parent-child OLD-AGE co-residence, reassessed in life-years. The homonym, and a careful one.
Old-age security motive for fertility, estimating what a co-resident family contributes to elderly poverty alleviation. C.3.c's, and the co-residence here is the elder-support kind.
